about: Modern IAF's voices: every speech clip of modern-iaf/data/sounds, made by `iaf-sim voices` (Kokoro text to speech, tools/iaf-2026/kokoro_tts.py, through crates/iaf-tools/src/sim_voices.rs: modern-iaf/docs/sound.md §5), the tower's phrase particles and templates (compiled by iaf-sim own into phraseparticalsdata.trx / phrasetemplates.trx, and each particle's Hebrew subtitle text_he into phraseparticles_he.trx, the format shared/audio/radio.gd reads, docs/radio.md §1). voices: each role's Kokoro voice and speed. clips: file, voice (the role), say (said in one pass), say_he (the Hebrew line, said by BlueTTS: `iaf-sim voices --he`, tools/iaf-2026/blue_tts.py, into he/<voice>/<file>), mode: betty (Betty's chain, said `repeat` times), radio (the radio chain with the key clicks), phrase / particle (the radio chain and hiss, no clicks: radio.gd frames the call with key_on / key_off); cut: the head or tail of `say` at its ';' by Kokoro's word timing. A particle key joined by '+' ("ALPHA_T+,+HOLD_POS") is one clip for that run of particles, which radio.gd plays in place of the run. In Hebrew a callsign is always its own clip (a joined key plays only where its clip exists in the language spoken), so a joined key with a callsign has no say_he, and he_only marks a joined key with only a Hebrew clip (the words after the callsign). role_he: the clip's Hebrew role where it differs from voice (none now: every call is in its speaker's role in both languages, modern-iaf/docs/sound.md §3.2).
